In this assignment, you'll be picking up where you left off with the M&Ms activity. You'll load the data and perform some basic statistical analysis. Follow the steps below to complete the assignment.

### Task 1: Load the tidyverse

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```



### Task 2: Load the M&Ms dataset from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv

```{r}
MMs <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv")
```



### Task 3: Sample 5 rows of data from the dataset

```{r}
set.seed(410)
sample_5 <- MMs |> sample_n(5)
```



### Task 4: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the sample, using either the red or black number of M&Ms

```{r}
  sample_5 |> 
   summarize(
     mean_red=mean(red),
     sd_red=sd(red))


     
   
```



### Task 5: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the population, using the same measure as in Task 4

```{r}
 MMs |> 
   summarize(
     mean_red=mean(red),
     sd_red=sd(red))
```



### Task 6: Compare the sample and population statistics

Both the mean and standard deviation of the full population are well above the mean and sd of the sample.The difference in mean is about 3.78,and the distance in standard deviation about 2.27.

### Task 7: Describe the results

Write a few sentences about what you found in the data. What does this tell you about the M&Ms dataset and about the act of random sampling?

I found that from the data, even the general totals had a large spread. There were samples all the way from 200-100, so taking plenty of samples would be important in order to correctly encapsulate the population as accurately as possible.

Even in my smaller sample, the totals ranged from 102 to 160. For just reds, one sample had 53 and one had 73.

Though the mean for red M&Ms in the sample ended up being 72.98, me landing one of the samples with 73 was pure luck, and that can't be relied on when trying to represent a population. Typically, the more samples you have the closer to full representation you will have in the data.
